note: Roadmap §1.4 gate. Per-method reference top-K recall and ranking-score regret for the cross-method optimizer benchmark. The bench is bit-deterministic per seed (identical output at 2 and at all threads), so these tolerances absorb intentional optimizer changes, not measurement noise. Regenerate with `cargo xtask optimizer-bench-check --write-baseline` after an intentional change, and say why in the PR. Rebaselined when capped candidate truncation became stratified (crew_generator round-robin over (captain, bridge pair) cells): score regret fell for both tiered lanes (tiered 0.00627 -> 0.00532, warm_start_tiered 0.00405 -> 0.00298) while recall@10 fell 0.36 -> 0.22. The recall drop is real, not a moved denominator — the reference sweep's cap does not bind on this case (638-660 crews generated against a cap of 800), so the reference set is byte-identical before and after. Tiered's confirmed crews now overlap the reference top-10 less while scoring as well or better; seed 11 is the clearest case, recall 0.8 -> 0.1 with regret unchanged at ~3e-5. KNOWN FINDING, not a passing grade: the stratified random control still reaches 0.0 score regret. Truncation was not the cause. The generator's whole proposal space for these params is those 638-660 crews and its best scores 0.9983, while random_stratified reaches 1.0 on all five seeds by sampling the full 189-captain / 242-bridge / 51-below-decks pools. Raising large_pool_captain_limit and large_pool_bridge_limit from 10/12 to 32/32 was measured and made tiered's regret worse at a fixed candidate budget, so closing the gap needs the budget and the proposal space widened together. `control_margin` stays wide enough to tolerate the known gap so the gate still catches a further regression; tracked in docs/OPTIMIZER_AMBITIOUS_ROADMAP.md §1.4.
